body:
Adds 32 agent rows, the identity probe, the `agent-mismatch` refusal, and the operator `probe_args`/`probe_match` fields.

The probe plumbing is sound. It runs only on a real launch, never under `--print`. It uses the launch environment with no stdin, a 5 s budget, and a 64 KiB cap. A failed probe refuses before any agent starts, and a passing probe lands in `launcher.json`.

Four rows are wrong. `kode`, `qoder`, `qodercn`, and `neovate` omit the print flag that the vendor docs cited in the row comments require for headless runs (`-p` or `-q`). Each launch therefore opens the interactive UI and runs into the watchdog. The argv tests in `agents_internal_test.go` pin the same wrong shape, so they pass while the rows stay broken.

The spec's open item for `cline` (confirm the prompt exits, or exclude the row) is not closed by the comment on that row.

comments.body: `kode` has no print flag, so the row launches the interactive UI. The docs this row cites run it headless only with `-p` (`kode -p "<prompt>"`, `-p, --print ... Print response and exit`). `qoder` (line 323) and `qodercn` (line 329) have the same gap: their run-in-scripts docs say `qoder -p "..."` and `qodercn -p "..."`. Add `Args: []string{"-p"}` to all three rows, then fix the pinned argv in `agents_internal_test.go`, which currently expects `kode --model M --x PROMPT`.

`neovate` is interactive by default. Its cited parser says `-q/--quiet` selects non-interactive mode, and the row has no `Args`. A launch therefore opens the TUI and times out with `agent-timeout`. Add `Args: []string{"-q"}`, and update the `neovate --model M --x PROMPT` expectation in `agents_internal_test.go` to match.

SPEC-2 §2 says `cline` must be confirmed to run a positional prompt once and exit, or be excluded with a reason. This comment confirms only that the prompt runs in yolo mode and that `-i` opens the TUI. The quoted reference never says the process exits after the turn, so that item is still `unproven`. Cite the line that shows exit, or drop the row. Otherwise a non-exiting `cline` ends in `agent-timeout`.

The `kilo` probe matches the bare text `run`, which almost any help screen contains. A different binary that prints `run` would pass the identity check and launch. The `fx` probe (`ask`) has the same weakness. Match on text only the intended CLI prints, such as its own usage line (`run [message..]` for kilo).

The usage-surface check is a plain substring match, so a short name passes on unrelated text. `pa` is satisfied by `agent-spawn-failed` in the usage text in `cmd/verdict/usage.go`, so deleting `pa` from the `--agent` list would still pass. Match the name as a token in the bracketed list, or compare against the list the usage line renders.
